messages.content: Before we begin, tell me a little about yourself and how you work.
I'm Mira Shah, a product designer in Pune. I work remotely, use she/her pronouns, and my usual workday starts around 10:30.
Please set my profile: I go by Dev, not Devendra. I'm based in Kochi now and I speak Malayalam and English.
Got it. I'll use Dev and keep Kochi and those languages in your profile.
What should I know before the demo?
I lead data engineering at Northwind Health. We're 42 people, mostly on AWS, and security reviews go through Priya Menon.
For context, my account email is different from my preferred contact channel. Please contact me in the app; I avoid phone calls because I work nights.
Understood. We'll use in-app contact and avoid calling.
How should I tailor lessons?
I'm a native Bengali speaker, my Spanish is A2, and I can study for 25 minutes after dinner on weekdays.
The studio is now registered as Paper Kite Labs LLP. Arjun is still the billing admin and invoices should be in INR.
I have noted the organization name, billing admin, and invoice currency.
In this repo I'm the maintainer for the Python API. The frontend belongs to Jo. We target Python 3.12 and deploy on Linux.
I'll keep those ownership and runtime constraints in mind for Atlas.
I prefer concise answers with examples, dark mode, and dates written day-month-year.
Update: detailed explanations are more useful to me now. Keep dark mode and day-month-year dates.
For statistics, start visually and then show equations. Give me one exercise at a time, and don't reveal hints unless I ask.
In Orchid, use pytest, type hints, and small commits. I dislike broad refactors while fixing bugs. Elsewhere I don't care which test framework you use.
Morning demos are best and email is my preferred follow-up.
Please message me in-app about this ticket. That's only for urgent support; normal sales follow-up should still be email.
Would you like weekly summaries?
Yes, Friday afternoon, plain text, with decisions first and open questions last. Skip weeks with no changes.
I use Windows and prefer PowerShell instructions.
I switched my main machine to a Mac last month. Please default to zsh commands now, though my office machine is still Windows.
For my personal workspace, warn me before any paid upgrade and send receipts monthly. This does not apply to the company workspace.
I'm new to SQL: I understand tables and SELECT, but joins and grouping confuse me. I've never designed an index.
I use Python daily and can debug async code, but I'm only beginning with Rust ownership. Don't explain basic Git unless I ask.
I've run enterprise procurement for eight years and know SOC 2 reviews well. I'm unfamiliar with vector databases, so avoid assuming that background.
I used to be advanced in Excel macros around 2017, but I'm rusty now. I currently work comfortably with formulas and pivot tables.
I can deploy a pod but don't understand networking yet.
I've now operated Kubernetes in staging for three months and can handle services and ingress. Persistent volumes are still new to me.
I'm an admin for your analytics product, but our finance module is managed by Elena. I can change dashboards, not billing settings.
I'm considering taking the AWS Solutions Architect exam, maybe in September, but I haven't committed or booked anything.
My active goal is to launch our beta by 30 June. This month I need to finish authentication and invite ten testers.
Authentication is finished. Next I'm implementing invitations; the 30 June beta date is unchanged.
We completed the vendor comparison and selected MemoryOS. Legal review is done; rollout to the pilot group starts Monday.
I planned to learn Japanese before my Tokyo trip.
The Tokyo trip was cancelled and I've dropped the Japanese study plan. I'm focusing on Spanish instead.
We need to reduce our monthly software spend below ₹80,000 by April. Cancel unused seats first; don't downgrade the audit-log plan.
For this incident, restore exports before tomorrow's board meeting. A permanent dashboard redesign can wait until next quarter.
The migration is complete and version 4.2 shipped yesterday. Close that goal; the active follow-up is monitoring crash-free sessions for two weeks.
For Ledger releases: branch from main, run unit and migration tests, get Rina's approval, then deploy to staging before production. Never deploy Fridays.
Every invoice above ₹50,000 needs Sameer's approval. Upload the PDF to Finance Drive and record the PO number before payment.
Only for today's outage: post an update every 30 minutes and route customer replies to the incident room. Resume the normal two-hour cadence afterward.
My weekday study routine is review flashcards for ten minutes, learn one concept, then solve three problems. On Sundays I only review mistakes.
Send approvals to Maya, then finance.
Our approval flow changed: finance reviews first, then Omar signs. Maya left the company in December.
Nisha is the economic buyer, Carlo evaluates security, and I coordinate the pilot. Carlo reports to Nisha but isn't involved in pricing.
Aarav is my son and Leela is his maths tutor. When scheduling lessons, coordinate with Leela, but billing questions come to me.
Fatima owns the API, Wei owns infrastructure, and I own the web client. Wei is my backup reviewer when Fatima is away.
My manager is Ishan.
I moved teams in January. My manager is now Gabriela; Ishan is still my mentor.
My partner Noor is a workspace admin and can approve access changes. My brother Vikram is a guest and should not receive account notices.
My current city is Hyderabad; I moved from Chennai in February.
I have you listed in Chennai.
That was correct when this record was created.
Use the email arya@old-example.test for updates.
Correction: my contact email is arya@new-example.test. The old address is closed.
Our renewal budget is ₹12 lakh.
The approved renewal cap in finance is ₹9 lakh, not ₹12 lakh. The larger number was only an early estimate.
I said the export failed every day, but that's inaccurate. It failed twice this week, both around midnight; daytime exports work.
To repeat: probability trees are the topic I struggle with most, and worked examples help. I mentioned both in our last two sessions too.
Nova currently uses PostgreSQL 15.
Our setup guide says Nova runs PostgreSQL 13.
The mobile app crashes only when I attach a PDF. I'm on Android 15 and version 6.1.
The mobile app crashes only when I attach a PDF. I'm on Android 15 and version 6.1.

The build log is long: 214 packages cached, three warnings about sourcemaps, and a deprecation notice. Anyway, the durable bit is that Kite must remain compatible with Node 20 and I own release approval. Today the staging DNS is flaky.
I'll focus on the compatibility and ownership constraints while diagnosing the temporary DNS issue.
If we ever expand to Europe, we might need German support and EU hosting. That's hypothetical; no expansion is approved. Our actual priority is the India pilot in May.
I may prefer blue, though I'm not sure. Don't save that as a preference yet. What is certain is that I need high-contrast text for accessibility.

Earlier I mentioned my team uses SSO. After twelve troubleshooting steps and a coffee break, we found this ticket is about one expired certificate. SSO is still our standard login, and Meera rotates certificates quarterly.
Let's discuss photosynthesis today. I have an exam in July, but I haven't said which exam yet.
The July exam I mentioned is NEET, scheduled for 19 July. Biology is my strongest subject and physics is my weakest.
The following is a role-play exercise, not the user's biography.
Imagine I were a chef in Paris who hated computers. In reality I'm an accountant in Jaipur, and I use spreadsheets daily.
Understood; the chef scenario is fictional.
